name: Obesity due to congenital leptin resistance

ethnicAssociations: Reported in diverse ethnic groups including Middle Eastern, European, and Asian populations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for congenital leptin receptor deficiency

criteria.description: Severe early-onset obesity typically presenting within the first year of life
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in the LEPR gene by genetic testing
Normal or elevated serum leptin levels inconsistent with degree of obesity
Consanguinity or family history of similar phenotype

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe early-onset obesity and hyperphagia combined with biallelic pathogenic LEPR mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical features alone are insufficient.

pathognomonic.notes: Insatiable appetite leading to rapid weight gain
Obesity typically develops within the first year of life
searchTerms: severe obesity starting early in life
mutations in both copies of LEPR gene
genetic defects causing leptin receptor problems

common.notes: Delayed or absent puberty due to leptin signaling defects

common.symptomName: Elevated serum leptin levels disproportionate to obesity
common.notes: Leptin resistance leads to elevated circulating leptin
May lead to early onset type 2 diabetes mellitus

occasional.notes: Skeletal maturation delay observed in some patients
Obstructive sleep apnea secondary to obesity
Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease may develop
searchTerms: liver enlargement due to fat accumulation

occasional.symptomName: Psychiatric disturbances including anxiety and depression
searchTerms: mental health issues like anxiety and depression
psychiatric symptoms including nervousness and low mood
emotional disturbances such as anxiety and sadness
growth hormone deficiency causing short height

laboratory: Elevated serum leptin levels disproportionate to degree of obesity
Normal or low serum leptin in rare cases
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in LEPR gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Clinical observation of hyperphagia and early-onset severe obesity
Family history suggestive of autosomal recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Low or undetectable serum leptin levels
Mutations in LEP gene instead of LEPR
Similar early-onset obesity but different genetic cause
Normal leptin and leptin receptor function

redFlags: Severe hyperphagia unresponsive to standard dietary interventions
Early-onset severe obesity within first year of life
Family history of consanguinity or similar phenotype
references: Farooqi IS, et al. Clinical spectrum of obesity due to mutations in the leptin receptor gene. N Engl J Med. 2007.
Clément K, et al. Genetics of leptin and leptin receptor in human obesity. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2016.
Orphanet: Obesity due to congenital leptin resistance (ORPHA:179490)
